description: Property-based evals for the MECE decomposition skill. Each case tests a specific dimension of output quality.

cases.description: Must anchor on Revenue = Volume × Price, not free-form business categories
cases.input: Why is revenue declining this quarter?
criteria: Top-level split maps to Volume and Price dimensions (exact words or clear synonyms like quantity/units, pricing/ASP/deal-size)
Does NOT use functional buckets (marketing, sales, product, engineering) at level 1
Sub-categories under Volume include churn/conversion/lead-related concepts
Sub-categories under Price include pricing/deal-size/mix concepts

cases.description: Must anchor on Profit = Revenue - Costs, not ad-hoc categories
criteria: Top-level split maps to Revenue side and Cost side
Does NOT jump straight to tactical categories (hiring, cloud spend, pricing) at level 1
Revenue side decomposes further (Volume × Price or similar)
Cost side decomposes into Fixed + Variable or similarly exhaustive split

cases.description: Given a domain where naive categories overlap, output must have clean boundaries
cases.input: What are all the ways we can reduce customer support ticket volume?
criteria: No category is a subset of another (e.g., 'improve documentation' and 'self-service' must not both appear as top-level peers)
Categories partition the space by a single consistent dimension (e.g., by ticket lifecycle stage, by root cause, or by intervention type — not a mix)
ME check section explicitly confirms no overlaps or explains boundary decisions
anti_patterns_at_level_1: improve product AND fix bugs as separate top-level items

cases.description: Decomposition must not miss obvious categories
cases.input: How do users leave our SaaS product?
criteria: Covers voluntary churn (user decides to leave)
Covers involuntary churn (payment failure, account expiry)
Covers contraction (user stays but downgrades/reduces usage)
CE check section confirms completeness or explains what was tested

cases.description: Complex problem should get 2-3 levels, not 1 (too shallow) or 5+ (over-decomposed)
cases.input: Why is our mobile app engagement declining?
criteria: Has at least 2 levels of decomposition
Does not exceed 3 levels for any branch
Leaf nodes are actionable or investigable (not further abstract categories)
High-impact branches get deeper decomposition than low-impact ones

cases.description: Every top-level category must have a rough size estimate
cases.input: What are all the sources of operational cost in our cloud infrastructure?
criteria: Every top-level category has an L/M/S size annotation
Sizing drives the 'where to focus' recommendation (largest bucket = recommended focus, or explicit reason if not)
At least one category is sized differently from others (not all Medium)

cases.description: Problem where 'Other' is tempting must be properly decomposed
cases.input: Categorize all the reasons a B2B sales deal might stall.
criteria: If an 'Other' category exists, it is clearly small/residual
No catch-all bucket like 'miscellaneous factors' or 'other reasons' captures more than one or two items
Major deal-stall reasons (budget, authority, need, timing, competition, internal politics) are all explicitly placed in named categories

cases.description: Must anchor on Latency = Network + Compute + I/O + Queue wait
cases.input: Why is our API response time so slow?
criteria: Top-level split maps to Network, Compute, I/O, and Queue/wait dimensions (exact words or clear synonyms)
Does NOT use symptom-based categories (slow database, bad code, too many users) at level 1
Each top-level category decomposes into specific investigable causes

cases.description: Must anchor on Bug source = Logic + Data + Concurrency + Integration + Environment
cases.input: What are all the possible root causes for this production bug?
criteria: Top-level split covers Logic, Data, Concurrency, Integration, and Environment dimensions (exact words or clear synonyms)
Does NOT use team-based categories (frontend bug, backend bug, infra bug) at level 1
Concurrency is explicitly present as its own category, not buried under Logic or Integration
Environment (config, OS, runtime version, etc.) is explicitly present, not lumped into other categories

cases.description: Must anchor on Attack surface = Network + Application + Identity + Data + Physical
cases.input: Where are we most vulnerable to a security breach?
criteria: Top-level split covers Network, Application, Identity, Data, and Physical dimensions
Does NOT use threat-actor categories (hackers, insiders, nation states) at level 1
Identity/authentication is its own category, not merged with Application
Physical security is included even for cloud-native contexts (supply chain, device theft, etc.)

cases.description: Output must follow the specified tree format with all required sections
cases.input: How can we improve developer productivity?
criteria: Uses tree notation (├── └── or equivalent indented structure)
Includes 'MECE Breakdown' header with problem statement
Includes ME check section
Includes CE check section
Includes 'Where to focus' recommendation
Top-level categories have L/M/S sizing annotations
No nested code block rendering issues
